goldens.comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.
The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.

Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.

An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:13 — url` is interpolated unescaped into `<a href='#{url}'>`; `'` is a valid URI char so an attacker-controlled embed_url like `http://host/x'onmouseover='alert(1)` passes URI()/host checks and becomes stored XSS in a raw_html post (survives Nokogiri re-serialization).

adjudication.rationale: In TopicEmbed.import, the code appends an HTML snippet containing `#{url}` directly into `contents` with no escaping. The only validation is `return unless url =~ /^https?\:\/\//`, which allows a `'` in the remainder of the URL. Because imported posts are created with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` and Post#cook returns `raw` unchanged for that mode, any injected attributes (e.g., `http://host/x'onmouseover='alert(1)`) would be stored and later rendered via `raw post.cooked` in the embed view. The subsequent Nokogiri fragment parsing in `absolutize_urls` does not sanitize attributes and would preserve an injected `onmouseover` attribute after re-serialization. This is a real stored-XSS vector introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:16 — Anyone who can send a forged Referer can enqueue an unbounded number of RetrieveTopic jobs with arbitrary embed_url values; the only throttle is per-URL inside the job, so unique query strings (`?x=1`, `?x=2`) bypass it, flood Sidekiq, amplify outbound fetches against embeddable_host, and create one new topic per unique URL under embed_by_username.

adjudication.rationale: In EmbedController#best, when no TopicEmbed exists for the provided embed_url, it unconditionally enqueues Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ..., embed_url: embed_url) with no rate limiting. The only throttling is later in TopicRetriever#retrieved_recently?, which keys on the full URL string ("retrieved:#{@embed_url}") so changing query strings (/path?x=1, ?x=2, ...) bypasses it. The Referer-based gate in ensure_embeddable relies on request.referer (a client-supplied header that can be forged by non-browser clients), so an attacker can repeatedly hit /embed/best with forged Referer and many unique embed_url values on the allowed host, flooding Sidekiq and triggering repeated remote fetches via TopicEmbed.import_remote(open(url).read), creating new topics per unique embed_url.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:20 — Race: two concurrent RetrieveTopic jobs both pass the `exists?` check, both run PostCreator (which publishes via MessageBus and enqueues process_post/notification jobs inside the outer `Topic.transaction`), then the second `TopicEmbed.create!` hits the unique index and rolls back the topic/post, leaving side-effect jobs pointing at a nonexistent post and an unhandled exception that Sidekiq retries.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `TopicEmbed.import`, it does `embed = TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` and, if blank, creates a new topic/post and then `TopicEmbed.create!` inside a transaction. With two concurrent callers for the same `url`, both can observe `embed.blank?` and both can successfully run `PostCreator.new(...).create` before the second hits the unique index on `topic_embeds.embed_url` at `TopicEmbed.create!`, raising (e.g.) `ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique` and aborting that transaction. The earlier `TopicRetriever.perform_retrieve` `exists?` check is also non-atomic and doesn’t prevent this. The diff therefore introduces a real race leading to an unhandled exception/job failure; the additional claim about MessageBus/enqueued jobs pointing to rolled-back posts depends on PostCreator internals not shown here, but the concurrency bug and resulting exception are directly implied by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:47 — open(url).read` via open-uri follows redirects to arbitrary hosts (including internal/link-local), so any redirector or open-redirect page on embeddable_host turns the referer-gated endpoint into SSRF against the Discourse network; no timeout or size cap either.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `TopicEmbed.import_remote` (app/models/topic_embed.rb around line 47), the code does `open(url).read` after only validating that the *initial* URL’s host matches `SiteSetting.embeddable_host` (via `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?`). `open-uri` follows HTTP redirects by default, and the code does not re-validate the final redirected host. So an open-redirect (or attacker-controlled page) on the allowed host can redirect the server to fetch arbitrary URLs (including internal/link-local), creating an SSRF vector. Additionally, there are no explicit timeouts or response size limits on the fetch, increasing DoS risk.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:47 — Readability is configured to keep `href`/`src` with no scheme filtering, and the result is stored as `cook_method: raw_html` bypassing Discourse sanitization, so `javascript:` links or other markup from the remote page (or any UGC page on embeddable_host) render unsanitized on the forum and in the iframe.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In TopicEmbed.import_remote, Readability::Document is configured to allow tags including `a`/`img` and attributes `href`/`src` with no visible scheme/protocol filtering. The extracted `doc.content` is then passed into TopicEmbed.import, which creates a post via PostCreator with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` and `skip_validations: true`. In Post#cook, `raw_html` returns `raw` directly, explicitly skipping the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline. The embed view also renders `<%= raw post.cooked %>`. Therefore any malicious markup (e.g., `<a href="javascript:...">`, `data:` URLs, or other unsafe HTML allowed by Readability) coming from the remote page on `embeddable_host` would be stored and rendered unsanitized, creating an XSS risk introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:34 — Feed item content (`CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content)`) is imported verbatim with zero sanitization into a raw_html post; any HTML/script in the feed becomes stored XSS for all forum readers.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb the code does `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` and passes it to `TopicEmbed.import`. `TopicEmbed.import` creates a post via `PostCreator` with `raw: absolutize_urls(url, contents)` and explicitly sets `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`. In Post#cook, `:raw_html` returns `raw` directly, skipping the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline. The embed view then renders with `<%= raw post.cooked %>`, so any HTML (including `<script>`/event handlers) from the feed would be stored and rendered to readers as-is, enabling stored XSS.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:39 — Every user-triggered RetrieveTopic for an unknown URL synchronously runs `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})`, so any unauthenticated request causes a full feed re-fetch and re-import (bypassing the hourly schedule and its `retry: false` isolation), multiplying the flood from the controller.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In lib/topic_retriever.rb `perform_retrieve` directly calls `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` whenever `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?` is true, before falling back to HTTP fetch. `TopicRetriever#retrieve` is invoked by the `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` job, which `EmbedController#best` enqueues whenever an embed is missing (`topic_id` nil) and it does so even when `current_user` is nil (anonymous) by passing `user_id: current_user.try(:id)`. This means embed-triggered requests can cause an immediate full feed poll outside the scheduled hourly `Jobs::PollFeed` run and without Sidekiq isolation/options (the `sidekiq_options retry: false` on the scheduled job is bypassed when calling `new.execute` directly). While there is a 60s Redis throttle keyed by `@embed_url`, varying unknown URLs can still force repeated feed polls.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:26 — setnx` then `expire` is non-atomic and the key is set before the fetch succeeds: a crash between the two calls leaves a permanent key that blocks the URL forever, and any fetch failure blocks retries for 60s while the loading page keeps reloading.

adjudication.rationale:
In lib/topic_retriever.rb#retrieved_recently? the throttle uses two separate Redis calls:

```rb
if $redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")
  $redis.expire(retrieved_key, 60)
  return false
end
```

This is non-atomic: if the process crashes after `setnx` but before `expire`, the key will exist without a TTL, effectively blocking future retrievals for that `@embed_url` indefinitely. Also, the throttle key is set before `perform_retrieve`/`fetch_http` runs, so a failed fetch still prevents another attempt for up to 60 seconds, while the embed loading page (app/views/embed/loading.html.erb) reloads every 30 seconds, potentially causing repeated “loading” despite failures. These behaviors are directly implied by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:34 — i.content` is nil for RSS feeds that use `description` (SimpleRSS only maps `content` for Atom/content:encoded), so `.scrub` raises NoMethodError and aborts the entire poll with `retry: false`.
matched_golden_ids: Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags that `i.content` can be nil for many RSS feeds (those using `description`), causing `.scrub` to raise NoMethodError and abort processing, and implies using a fallback. This is the same nil-content crash issue described in the golden comment.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:22 — PostCreator#create` returns nil on failure and errors are discarded without logging, so import failures (and the resulting infinite 30s reload loop in loading.html.erb) are completely silent.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the new-topic path does `creator = PostCreator.new(...); post = creator.create` inside a transaction, but if `post` is blank/nil it simply skips creating the `TopicEmbed` record and returns `post` (nil) with no logging or error propagation (`if post.present? ... end` has no `else`). Separately, `EmbedController#best` renders `loading` whenever `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` is nil, and `app/views/embed/loading.html.erb` unconditionally reloads every 30s. So if the background retrieval/import never creates the embed (including the “post is blank” case), the user experience is an endless reload with no indication of why the import failed.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/views/embed/loading.html.erb:8 — Loading page reloads every 30s forever with no cap; combined with the enqueue-on-every-request controller path, each stuck embed becomes a perpetual job generator for as long as the tab is open.

adjudication.rationale: In app/views/embed/loading.html.erb the script does `setTimeout(function() { document.location.reload(); }, 30000);` with no termination condition, so the page will reload every 30 seconds indefinitely as long as the tab stays open. In EmbedController#best, when `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` returns nil, it unconditionally executes `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ... embed_url: embed_url)` and renders `loading`. Therefore, if the embed never becomes available (e.g., retrieval fails), each reload triggers another enqueue, creating a perpetual stream of Sidekiq jobs for that embed URL.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:42 — Test mocks `TopicRetriever.new` but the controller only calls `Jobs.enqueue`; it passes solely because test env runs jobs inline, so it silently stops exercising the code path if queueing is enabled and never tests the referer-forgery/host mismatch case for embed_url.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/controllers/embed_controller.rb#best`, when no existing embed is found it calls `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)` and renders `loading`; it does **not** instantiate `TopicRetriever` directly. However `spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb` (the “tells the topic retriever to work…” example) sets expectations on `TopicRetriever.new` and `retriever.retrieve` being called during the request. That expectation is not aligned with the controller code path and would only be satisfied if `Jobs.enqueue` causes the job to execute synchronously/inline in the test environment (via external test configuration), making the spec fragile and not truly verifying the controller behavior (enqueueing the job).

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:63 — href.start_with?('/')` also matches protocol-relative `//other.host/path`, which is rewritten to `http://host/other.host/path`, silently corrupting cross-host links and images.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls`, both link and image rewriting treat any `href`/`src` that `start_with?('/')` as a same-host relative path and rewrite it as `#{prefix}/#{href.sub(/^\/+/, '')}`. A protocol-relative URL like `//other.host/path` also starts with `/`, so it will be rewritten to something like `http://<currenthost>/other.host/path`, which corrupts the intended cross-host URL. The same logic applies to `img` `src` values.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:17 — Origin check `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` is a substring test, so an origin like `http://a` or a prefix of discourseUrl passes and can drive iframe height from any frame.
matched_golden_ids: The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both comments flag the same flaw: validating message origin via `indexOf`/substring matching is insecure and can be bypassed by attacker-controlled origins that are substrings/prefixes of the allowed URL (e.g., lookalike domains).

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb:3 — Adding `force: true` to an already-shipped migration makes it drop an existing `top_topics` table with data on any DB where the migration is re-run or was never recorded.

adjudication.rationale: The diff modifies an existing migration (`20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb`) to use `create_table :top_topics, force: true`. In Rails, `force: true` will drop the table if it already exists before creating it. This changes behavior from “fail if table exists” to “silently drop and recreate”, which can cause data loss on any database where the migration is executed while `top_topics` already exists (e.g., migration history missing/corrupt, manual table creation, or re-running the migration). This is a real, concrete risk introduced by the change in the diff.
